intro: The following summary presents the shift‑wise difficulty and attempt patterns for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam held on 11 October 2026. Information is drawn from candidate reports and video analyses, and therefore the figures are unofficial. The SSC normally normalises scores across shifts to ensure comparability. Where only partial data is available, the analysis reflects the limited evidence and may be updated as more reports emerge.

faqs.q: What overall difficulty was reported for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 11 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was described as ranging from Easy to Moderate, Shift 2 was reported as Easy across all sections, and most reports for Shift 3 also labelled the exam as Easy. The difficulty assessments therefore vary slightly between shifts.

faqs.q: How many good attempts were recorded for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 11 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 had good attempts reported around 17‑18 questions overall. Reliable figures for good attempts were not provided for Shifts 2 and 3, so no definitive numbers can be given for those shifts.

faqs.q: Is a complete analysis available for Shift 2 of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 11 October 2026?
faqs.a: Only partial information has been published for Shift 2. The available data suggests an overall Easy difficulty, but a full analysis is not yet usable and more evidence is needed.

faqs.q: How does the SSC compare scores across the three shifts of the 11 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: The SSC normalises scores across shifts, applying a standardisation process that adjusts raw marks to a common scale so that candidates from different shifts can be compared fairly.

faqs.q: Are the figures presented for the 11 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 exam official?
faqs.a: No. The numbers are unofficial and are based on candidate‑submitted reports and media coverage. Official results will be released by the SSC after the examination process is completed.
